Off-By-One (OBO) count error. If the predicted count is within one count of the ground truth value, then the video is considered to be classified correctly, otherwise it is a misclassification.
The OBO error is the mis-classification rate over the entire dataset.

Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of count. This metric measures the absolute difference between the ground truth count and the predicted count, and then normalizes it by dividing with the ground truth count.

We observe that a common failure mode of our model is that for some actions (e.g. juggling soccer ball), it predicts half the count reported by annotators.
This happens when the model considers left and right legs’ motion for counting while people tend to consider the ball’s up/down motion resulting in people double counting the repetitions.
